The triangle \(ABC\) has sides \(AB = 17\), \(AC = 8\), and \(BC = 15\). Since \(8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17^2\), it is a right triangle with the right angle at \(C\). The area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 15 = 60\).

The altitude from \(C\) to hypotenuse \(AB\) creates two smaller right triangles, \(\triangle ACD\) and \(\triangle BCD\), both similar to \(\triangle ABC\). \(\triangle ACD\) shares angle \(A\) with \(\triangle ABC\), so the similarity ratio is \(\frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{8}{17}\). The ratio of their areas is the square of the similarity ratio:

\[
\text{Area}(\triangle ACD) = \left(\frac{8}{17}\right)^2 \times \text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = \frac{64}{289} \times 60 = \frac{3840}{289}.
\]

Answer: \(\frac{3840}{289}\)
